title: Scheduling Construction, Installments and Setting the Meter — Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
On a **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** project, Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative's operations rule for scheduling construction, collecting the rest of the contribution and setting the meter is as follows.

## Scheduling

Construction is scheduled only when payments reach the class's percent of the contribution required before scheduling, every recorded easement is on file where the class requires easements, and the project is in contract signed status. The judgement rests on the project's own records: the contribution on the project, the payments recorded on it, whether every required recorded easement has been received, and the project's status. When construction is scheduled the project moves to scheduled status and the scheduled date is recorded.

| Payments have reached the required percent of the contribution | Every recorded easement on file (where the class requires easements) | Project in contract signed status | Construction may be scheduled under this rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Yes | No | Yes | No |
| Yes | Yes | No | No |

On a class that does not require easements, the second column does not apply.

"Reach" includes equality. On a hypothetical $12,000.00 contribution with 25 percent required before scheduling, payments of $3,000.00 reach the requirement and payments of $2,999.99 do not; with 100 percent required, payments must reach the whole $12,000.00.

## Installments

Where the class allows installments, the rest of the contribution is paid in up to the class's most monthly installments, in equal monthly installments invoiced on the project. On the hypothetical $12,000.00 contribution with $3,000.00 paid before scheduling and a class allowing up to 12 installments, the $9,000.00 rest may be invoiced as 12 equal monthly installments of $750.00, or as fewer equal monthly installments.

## Setting the meter

The meter is set only when a state electrical inspection certificate dated no more than the class's certificate validity days before the energize date is on file, where the class requires the certificate. With a 180-day limit, a certificate dated 180 days before the energize date is on file in time, and one dated 181 days before it is not.

## Energization

Energization is targeted within the class's energizing target in business days of scheduling and starts billing on the pending service account. When construction is completed and the meter set, the project moves to energized status and the energized date is recorded.
